notes.decision: Fits with guardrails. The sign-in page itself says the platform is upgrading, on arrival, and the auth error boundary asks the platform before blaming the page. No proxy or transport change; the hold has no controls and retries on the server's cadence.
notes.persona: A person who opens the portal during a self-upgrade reads one sentence that says what is happening and that nothing is needed from them, and is signed in normally a few minutes later without touching anything.
notes.reuse: Composes Surface. The quiescence truth comes from the existing allow-listed state route the proxy already reads; the server render uses the existing getQuiescenceConfig.
notes.sourceTruth: PlatformConfig quiescence level and run id via getQuiescenceConfig on the server and /api/internal/quiescence-state in the browser. Nothing is stored client-side.
notes.states: Normal: unchanged sign-in form. Draining or swapping on arrival: the hold instead of the form. Submit that raced the drain: the boundary probes and shows the hold instead of the generic card; a probe failure is unknown and keeps the generic card. Run id shown as text for support; no colour-only meaning; role=status, aria-live=polite.
notes.aiBoundary: No coworker prompt; nothing is sent anywhere but the platform's own state route.
notes.verification: Unit tests: the hold's copy and self-resume on the retry cadence, the boundary choosing the hold only when quiescing, the page rendering the hold instead of the form while draining (10/10 with the error-card suite). Live verification: the next governed self-upgrade on this install is the real check and is recorded on the backlog item when it happens; until then the UX check is reported as unit-verified, not live-verified.
